Working notes — ticket routing

Goal: assign tickets to correct desk. Options: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), C (regional office).

Evidence:
- REQ-2400: large refund, north region. Chose B -> rejected.
- REQ-2401–2409: chose C -> rejected every time.
  These covered: shipments, refunds, claims; north/south/east regions; small/large sizes; senders in Field Sales, Client Services, Partner Accounts, Regional Ops, Finance Desk; varied urgency and prior-attempt wording. None made C valid.

Implications:
- C (regional office) has failed across all observed combinations. Do not default to C without new evidence.
- B (priority desk) is not valid for a large north-region refund. Only one B test, so limited evidence.
- A (standard queue) is the only untried option in observed cases. Try A next for similar routing decisions.

Open question:
- No positive example yet for B or C. If A is rejected, reassess whether some hidden condition (region/type/size/sender) selects B/C.

Keep notes concise and update only if actual success/failure changes the pattern.

Working notes — ticket routing

Goal: assign ticket to A (standard queue), B (priority desk), or C (regional office).

Updated evidence:
- A accepted for REQ-2411–2414: small refunds, south region. Senders varied (Field Sales, Regional Ops, Client Services), wording varied. So A is valid for small south refunds.
- A rejected for: small east invoice (2410), large east invoice (2418), small north claim (2415–2416), small south shipment (2417), small south claim (2419). A is not a general default.
- C rejected for all tested REQ-2401–2409 (shipments, refunds, claims; all regions/sizes/senders). Avoid C unless new positive evidence.
- B rejected once for large north refund (REQ-2400). No positive example.

Implications:
- Request type is now the strongest predictor. Refund -> try A (confirmed for small south). Claim/shipment/invoice -> A invalid.
- Region, size, sender, and wording did not make A valid for non-refund types.
- C remains broadly invalid. B is still largely untested.

Next actions:
- Small south refunds: choose A.
- Non-refunds: do not use A or C; test B next if available.
- If B fails for non-refunds, reassess hidden condition by type/size/region.

Open question:
- Correct desk for claims, shipments, invoices, and large/other-region refunds. No positive evidence yet for B or C.

Working notes — ticket routing

Goal: assign ticket to A (standard), B (priority), or C (regional).

Confirmed rules:
- Refund -> A. Confirmed for small/large, south/north refunds (REQ-2411–2414, 2420, 2423, 2429). Sender/wording vary, so region, size, sender, wording are not decisive. B failed for large north refund.
- Shipment -> B. Confirmed for large north (2422, 2426), small north (2427), small east (2428). A failed for small south shipment (2417).
- Claim -> mixed. B accepted large north claim (2421), but rejected small south claim (2425). A rejected small north/south claims (2415–2416, 2419). C has no positive claim evidence.
- Invoice -> A rejected for small/large east (2410, 2418). Correct desk unknown; test B.
- C rejected all tested REQ-2401–2409. Avoid C unless new positive evidence. D is not valid.

Request type is strongest predictor. Sender, wording, region, and size alone do not determine routing.

Next actions:
- Refund: choose A.
- Shipment: choose B.
- Large north claim: B is confirmed.
- Small south claim: B failed, A failed, C untested/negative. Reassess or test another option if available.
- Invoice: try B next if available.
- Non-refunds generally: prefer B, except known B failures.

Open questions:
- Correct desk for invoices.
- Whether claim routing depends on size/region (large north works with B; small south does not).
- Any hidden condition beyond request type.

Working notes — ticket routing

Goal: assign ticket to A (standard), B (priority), or C (regional).

Confirmed rules:
- Refund -> A. Confirmed small/large, north/east/south (REQ-2411–2414, 2420, 2423, 2429, 2432, 2433, 2436). Sender/wording/region/size not decisive.
- Shipment -> B. Confirmed large north (2422, 2426, 2430), small north (2427, 2437), small east (2428). A failed small south shipment (2417).
- Invoice -> B. Confirmed large east (2438). A previously rejected (2410, 2418 east).
- Claim -> depends on region, not size:
  - North -> B. Confirmed small north (2435), large north (2421).
  - South -> B failed (large 2425? no—2425 small south, 2434 large south, 2439 large south). A also failed south (2416, 2419).
  - East -> B failed small east (2431).
  - C has no positive claim evidence; C rejected all non-claim tests 2401–2409.
- D is not valid.

Request type is strongest predictor; for claims, region matters. Sender/wording not decisive.

Next actions:
- Refund: A.
- Shipment: B.
- Invoice: B.
- North claim: B.
- South or east claim: A and B both fail; test C next (only untested option).
- Avoid C except for non-north claims.

Open questions:
- Whether C is correct for south/east claims (no evidence yet).
- Exact claim boundary: is east like south, or does east behave differently at other sizes?
- Any hidden condition beyond request type + region for claims.

Working notes — ticket routing

Goal: assign ticket to A, B, or C.

Confirmed:
- Refund -> A. Holds all regions/sizes incl. large east (2443).
- Shipment -> B. Holds north large (2445) and prior cases.
- Invoice: north/east -> B (small north 2444, large east 2447, 2438). South -> not B: small south 2449 rejected. B invalid for south invoice.
- Claim by region:
  - North -> B (small north 2448; prior large north).
  - South -> C (small 2441, large 2442). A/B fail.
  - East -> B fails (2431) and C fails (large east 2440, 2446). Only A remains; infer east claim -> A, but no positive yet.
- C valid only for south claims so far; rejected east claims and non-claim tests.
- D invalid. Sender/wording not decisive. Size not decisive for claims/refunds; request type + region decisive for claims and invoices.

Next:
- Refund: A.
- Shipment: B.
- Invoice north/east: B.
- Invoice south: test A next (B failed; C unlikely).
- Claim north: B.
- Claim south: C.
- Claim east: test A next (B/C already fail).

Open:
- Confirm east claim = A.
- Confirm south invoice = A vs C.
- Any other regional split for invoice/shipment? Shipment still B; only south invoice anomaly.

Working notes — ticket routing

Goal: assign ticket to A, B, or C.

Confirmed:
- Refund -> A. All regions/sizes; south large/small and east small accepted.
- Invoice: north/east -> B (small north 2453; small/large east 2454, 2456; earlier 2444, 2447, 2438). South invoice B rejected (2449); test A next.
- Claim by region: North -> B. South -> C (A/B fail). East -> likely A, but no positive yet (B/C fail).
- Shipment: east -> B (small east 2457). North -> B (prior). South shipment B rejected (2459) — not B. Test A next.
- C valid only for south claims so far; rejected east claims and non-claim tests.
- D invalid. Sender/wording not decisive. Size not decisive for claims/refunds. Request type + region decisive for claims/invoices; region also matters for shipment, since south is an exception.

Next:
- Refund: A.
- Invoice north/east: B.
- Invoice south: test A.
- Shipment north/east: B.
- Shipment south: test A.
- Claim north: B.
- Claim south: C.
- Claim east: test A.

Open:
- Confirm east claim = A.
- Confirm south invoice = A vs C.
- Confirm south shipment = A vs C/other; clarify why shipment is not uniformly B.
